name: Cochleosaccular Degeneration-Cataract Syndrome

criteria.description: Bilateral sensorineural hearing loss due to cochleosaccular degeneration
Presence of bilateral cataracts, typically developing in childhood or early adulthood
Audiometric testing confirming progressive sensorineural hearing loss
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of bilateral sensorineural hearing loss with cochleosaccular degeneration and bilateral cataracts
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by audiometric and ophthalmological findings; genetic testing may assist if causative mutation identified.

searchTerms: hearing loss that worsens over time

laboratory: Exclusion of metabolic causes of cataract and hearing loss
imaging: MRI may show cochlear and vestibular nerve degeneration
Ocular ultrasound to assess lens opacity
genetic: Possible mutations in genes associated with cochleosaccular degeneration and cataract formation (e.g., connexin genes, crystallin genes)
other: Audiometric testing confirming sensorineural hearing loss

distinguishingFeatures: Isolated hearing loss without ocular involvement
Presence of cataract with systemic features other than hearing loss
Progressive vision loss with hearing impairment

redFlags: Rapid progression of hearing loss in early childhood
Sudden onset of visual impairment due to cataract
Family history of early deafness and cataract
references: Smith RJH, et al. Genetic Hearing Loss Overview. GeneReviews. 2020.
Heckenlively JR, et al. Hereditary Hearing Loss and Deafness Overview. GeneReviews. 2019.
